entries.def:
δαιμονιώδης, -ες
(δαιμόνιον, εἶδος), [in Sm.: Psa.91.6 * ;] 
demon-like: Jas.3.15 (Cremer, 171).†
(AS)

δαίμων, -ονος, ὁ, ἡ 
[in LXX for גַּד, Isa.65.11 (א; δαιμονίῳ, AB) * ;] 
in cl. and NT = δαιμόνιον; a demon: Mat.8.31.†
(AS)

δάκνω 
[in LXX for נשׁךְ, Gen.49.17, al., exc. Deu.8.15 (שׂרף) ;] 
to bite: metaphorically, Gal.5.15.†
(AS)

δάκρυον (poët. form δάκρυ), -ου, τό, 
[in LXX for דִּמְעָה ;] 
a tear: Mrk.9.24 (WH, txt., R, txt. omit), Act.20.19, 31, 2Co.2.4, 2Ti.1.4, Heb.5.7; 12.17, Rev.7.17; 21.4; metaphorically, dative pl., δάκρυσι (Lam.2.11, Thuc., vii, 75; Bl., § 9, 3), Luk.7.38, 44.†
(AS)

δακρύω 
[in LXX for בָּכָה, etc. ;] 
to weep, shed tears: Jhn.11.35.†
SYN.: κλαίω, of audible weeping, to cry; ὀδύρομαι, of grief expressed verbally, to lament; θρηνέω, of formal lamentation, to sing a dirge; ἀλαλάζω, to wail in Oriental fashion; στενάζω, of grief expressed by inarticulate sounds, to groan. (AS)

δακτύλιος, -ου, ὁ
(δάκτυλος), [in LXX chiefly for טַבַּעַת ;] 
a ring: Luk.15.22.†
(AS)

δάκτυλος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for אֶצְבַּע ;] 
a finger: Mat.23.4, Mrk.7.33, Luk.11.46; 16.24, Jhn.8.6, 8; 20.25, 27; metaphorically, δ. θεοῦ (cf. Exo.8.19), Luk.11.20.†
(AS)

Δαλμανουθά, ἡ
indecl., 
Dalmanutha, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee: Mrk.8.10 (cf. Μαγαδάν).†
(AS)

Δαλματία (L, Δελ-), -ας, ἡ 
Dalmatia, a part of Illyria on E. coast of the Adriatic: 2Ti.4.10.†
(AS)
